rubrics.evidence: In update_region_mapping, the agent patch deletes the inlined per-window X transitions (xcb_map_window/xcb_unmap_window of frame/id/debug, mapping/unmapping counters, mapped flag, and WM_STATE restamp via a_state) and replaces them with calls to window-side helpers: map_window(w) for the map branch and unmap_window(w) for the unmap branch, with the ws_win w as the owner argument.
rubrics.criterion: In spectrwm.c, the mapping refresh (update_region_mapping and its update_mapping caller path) no longer performs a window's map or unmap transition itself: the per-window X transition -- map/unmap of the frame, the client window and the debug window, the mapping/unmapping counters, the mapped flag and the paired WM_STATE restamp with the a_state property change -- is now carried out by code hosted on the window record (a function whose owner parameter is the ws_win being transitioned), whatever that function is named in the repair.

rubrics.evidence: The refactor request asked to move per-window map/unmap behavior back to the window side while leaving drivers to decide which windows a region shows. In update_region_mapping, the agent patch keeps the region coordinator logic intact: it still derives `ws = r->ws` and `bar = r->bar`, computes `wf` and `mof`, and uses the same visibility gates (`!HIDDEN(w) && (!mof || (w && wf && w->main == wf->main) || WINDOCK(w))` for mapping; `HIDDEN(w) || (mof && !(w && wf && w->main == wf->main) && !WINDOCK(w))` for unmapping). It still walks only `ws->winlist` with two `TAILQ_FOREACH` loops in the same map-then-unmap visit order. The only change is replacing the inlined transition/restamp code with calls to `map_window(w)` and `unmap_window(w)`, re-homing the transition without moving the visibility decision.
rubrics.criterion: After the repair, update_region_mapping still performs its coordinator job for exactly its own region: it derives the region's workspace and visibility filter (the mof/main-identity and WINDOCK gating), walks only that region's window list, and triggers each window's transition in the same visit order -- the repair re-homes the transition, not the visibility decision.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch only touches update_region_mapping, replacing inlined map/unmap WM_STATE restamping with map_window(w)/unmap_window(w). It does not modify focus() at all, so the dispatcher still contains the inlined focus_redirect chain chase and the inlined urgency probe (SWM_Q_IGNOREURGENT gate plus xcb_icccm_wm_hints_get_urgency/DEMANDS_ATTENTION) from smell.diff; those window-side resolution steps are not delegated to window-owned code paths.
rubrics.criterion: In the focus keybinding dispatch (focus in spectrwm.c), resolving a focus candidate no longer re-implements the window-side resolution steps field-by-field inside the dispatcher: following a candidate's main/focus_redirect chain (bounded in the same way and stopping on NULL, hidden or invalid targets) and probing a candidate's urgency (the SWM_Q_IGNOREURGENT quirks gate before the WM_HINTS urgency and demands-attention test) are performed by window-owned code paths, so the dispatcher seeds candidates per binding path and hands the resolved window over to focus setting.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch only modifies update_region_mapping, replacing inlined map/unmap code with map_window(w)/unmap_window(w). It does not touch the focus-family stacking-layer recomputation introduced in smell.diff inside focus(), where the dispatcher computes layer values via raised/desktop/below/fullscreen/maximized/dock/floating/tiled precedence and writes redirect->st->layer = layer and lw->st->layer = layer for related windows. That per-window layer logic remains dispatcher-owned, so the rubric is not satisfied.
rubrics.criterion: The stacking-layer recomputation for the focus family after a focus change -- deciding each family window's layer from raised/desktop/below/fullscreen/maximized/dock/floating/tiled in that precedence, applying the rule that a related window stays at or above its main's layer, and stamping the resulting layer -- is window-owned code after the repair; the dispatcher only identifies the family (the main window and its related windows) rather than computing and writing layer values itself.

rubrics.evidence: The agent.patch only modifies update_region_mapping(), replacing inlined map/unmap code with map_window(w)/unmap_window(w). It contains no changes to iconify() or the hide/focus-drop path. The smell.diff shows iconify() still inlines the focus-drop logic in the keybinding handler: validate_win/kill_refs cleanup, setting win->s->focus = NULL, clearing win->ws->focus and win->ws->focus_raise, calling update_win_layer/refresh_stack/update_stacking only when raise is true, and the minimal-border floating check with update_gravity() and X/Y adjustment. Since that logic remains re-implemented in the handler rather than delegated to window-owned code, the rubric fails.
rubrics.criterion: In the iconify/hide path, dropping focus from the targeted window -- the invalid window/workspace validation with dangling-reference cleanup, clearing the screen's focus mirror and the workspace's focus/focus_raise mirrors under the same conditions, re-deriving stacking and priority only when always_raise or focus_raise demands it, and the minimal-border floating check with its border/gravity adjustment -- is performed by window-owned code rather than re-implemented inside the keybinding handler.

rubrics.evidence: The rubric requires the hide/hide-state EWMH transition to be owned by the window side, but agent.patch only delegates the map/unmap WM_STATE restamp in update_region_mapping by replacing inlined code with map_window(w)/unmap_window(w). It does not touch the iconify handler, where smell.diff shows the EWMH state machine was re-implemented inline: manual EWMH_F_HIDDEN flip, TAILQ_INSERT_HEAD/TAILQ_REMOVE iconified-list sync, load_float_geom/store_float_geom transitions, EWMH_F_MAXIMIZED clearing, and a rebuilt _NET_WM_STATE atom set written via xcb_change_property/xcb_delete_property. Those flag-word writes and atom rebuild remain in the driver/handler, so the EWMH state machine is not moved back to one window-side code path.
rubrics.criterion: Applying the hide/hide-state flag flip to a window still keeps the whole EWMH state machine on one code path owned by the window side: flipping EWMH_F_HIDDEN, keeping iconified-list membership in sync with it, reloading or storing floating geometry on the transitions (unhide reload for floating windows, above/below and maximized/fullscreen geometry bookkeeping), clearing EWMH_F_MAXIMIZED under the same condition, and rebuilding the _NET_WM_STATE atom set from the window's full flag word before publishing to the window's X window.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch only touches update_region_mapping: it removes that function's inlined map/unmap+WM_STATE blocks and replaces them with map_window(w)/unmap_window(w). It does not modify focus or iconify, so the duplicated redirect chase, urgency test, layer precedence chain, focus-drop guard chain, and EWMH flag-flip/atom-rebuild statements introduced in smell.diff remain inside those driver functions.
rubrics.criterion: The re-implemented transition code inside the three driver functions is genuinely removed rather than bypassed: after the repair no duplicated copy of the map/unmap+WM_STATE statements, the redirect chase, the urgency test, the layer precedence chain, the focus-drop guard chain, or the flag-flip/atom-rebuild statements remains inside focus, update_region_mapping or iconify -- each exists exactly once, in its owner-side home.

rubrics.evidence: The patch only modifies update_region_mapping, replacing the inlined map/unmap blocks with calls to map_window(w) and unmap_window(w). It does not touch transfer_win/send_to_rg, switch_workspace, stack, raise_focus, or maximize-toggle paths, so those collaborators retain their existing sequencing and helper usage unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: The window-transition code paths that other flows use remain coherent after the repair: window transfer/move (transfer_win/send_to_rg paths), workspace switching and stacking (switch_workspace, stack and raise-path callers such as raise_focus and the maximize-related toggles) still reach the same owner-side transition implementations the drivers now delegate to, and perform their own sequencing (focus seeding, apply_unfocus, stacking refresh, mapping update) exactly as before.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch's only hunk is in update_region_mapping, replacing inlined map/unmap blocks with map_window(w)/unmap_window(w); it does not touch iconify's replacement-focus mode split, so the nfw==NULL && win_free(win) current-region resolution and the final if (!follow && nfw) { ... set_focus(s, redirect); } handoff remain unchanged, preserving exactly one set_focus per activation.
rubrics.criterion: After hiding a window, the replacement focus resolution keeps the two modes intact: when pointer follow applies, the replacement candidate resolved from the current region is chased through its own redirect chain before focus is set; when pointer follow does not apply, no replacement is forced on the user and the direct focus handoff happens exactly once per activation.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch only removes the inlined map/unmap and WM_STATE restamp blocks from update_region_mapping and restores map_window(w)/unmap_window(w) calls; it adds no new locals and removes the inner uint32_t data[2] temporaries. rubrics.evidence: The patch only restores map_window/unmap_window in update_region_mapping, removing the inlined mapping/state DNPRINTF and WM_STATE restamp duplicates there. rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the inlined xcb_map_window/xcb_unmap_window plus xcb_change_property(a_state) transition code from update_region_mapping and restores calls to the existing window-side helpers map_window(w) and unmap_window(w). rubrics.criterion: The repair does not decouple ICCCM WM_STATE from the X transition: no code path maps or unmaps a window without restamping its WM_STATE as NORMAL or ICONIC in the same operation, and no path restamps state without performing the corresponding map/unmap -- in particular reparented windows (frame != XCB_WINDOW_NONE) keep the skip behavior exactly as before.

rubrics.evidence: The patch only refactors update_region_mapping to call map_window()/unmap_window(); it does not touch iconify, where the EWMH_F_HIDDEN flag flip and the TAILQ_INSERT_HEAD/TAILQ_REMOVE on the iconified list remain in the same `if (changed & EWMH_F_HIDDEN)` block, so no path flips the hidden flag without updating the list and both changes stay in one hide/unhide operation.
rubrics.criterion: Iconified-list membership keeps mirroring the window's hidden flag exactly: a window is inserted on hide (and unmapped together with its frame/debug windows) and removed on unhide (with floating geometry reloaded for windows that float), with no path that flips the flag without updating the list or vice versa, and both changes remain part of one hide/unhide operation.

rubrics.evidence: The diff only touches update_region_mapping. It leaves the map/unmap guard conditions unchanged (map: !HIDDEN(w) && (!mof || (w && wf && w->main == wf->main) || WINDOCK(w)); unmap: HIDDEN(w) || (mof && !(w && wf && w->main == wf->main) && !WINDOCK(w))) and replaces the inlined WM_STATE restamp with map_window(w)/unmap_window(w). It does not modify the focus/iconify guard chains from smell.diff (urgency quirk check, redirect-chase NULL/hidden/invalid stop bounded by count_win(... SWM_COUNT_NORMAL), validation-before-clearing, minimal-border five-condition test), so no short-circuit order is reordered or weakened.
rubrics.criterion: The re-homed code does not reorder or weaken the evaluation order of the guard chains: validation of the targeted window and its workspace (and the dangling-reference cleanup it triggers) still precedes any focus-mirror clearing; urgency is still evaluated only for windows whose quirks do not ignore it; the redirect chase still stops at the first NULL, hidden or invalid target and remains bounded by the workspace's normal-window count; the minimal-border geometry adjustment still tests the same five floating conditions with short-circuiting.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch only restores map_window/unmap_window in update_region_mapping; it leaves the inlined focus-family layer computation in focus() untouched. That block stamps redirect=winfocus->main once, then TAILQ_FOREACH over winfocus->ws->winlist with lw->main==winfocus->main stamps the main again (the main is in the winlist and matches its own main), double-stamping the main window's layer in one refresh and violating the 'exactly once' / 'no layer stamped twice' requirement.
rubrics.criterion: After delegation, layer computation produces the same values as before for every window of the focus family: the precedence order raised, desktop, below, fullscreen, maximized, dock, floating, tiled is unchanged, a non-main window never ends below its main's already-stamped layer, the family walk covers the main window exactly once and then every related window of the same main exactly once per focus change, and no layer is stamped twice for the same window in one refresh.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the inlined map/unmap and WM_STATE restamp logic from update_region_mapping and restores calls to the existing window-side helpers map_window(w) and unmap_window(w), which take a ws_win* as their owner parameter. No new function is introduced, and no screen/region parameter is threaded through a helper to drive a window's transitions, so the foreign-owner coupling is not recreated elsewhere.
rubrics.criterion: The repair does not recreate the same foreign-owner coupling elsewhere: code moved out of the three drivers ends up hosted by the data it operates on (window-side state as window-owned parameters), rather than being parked on a new global-style home or on the screen/region side wholesale -- in particular no new function keeps doing a window's transitions while carrying the screen or region as its owner parameter.
